definition: Vaex is an out-of-core DataFrame library that explores billions of rows using memory-mapping and lazy expressions.
details: Created by Maarten Breddels and Jovan Veljanoski; developed by the company Vaex.io.

explainer.lead: How to install Vaex, a first working example, and where it fits in an AI project.
explainer.createdBy: Created by Maarten Breddels and Jovan Veljanoski (Vaex.io).

quickstart.python:
import vaex

df = vaex.open("big.hdf5")              # memory-mapped, not loaded
df["ratio"] = df.clicks / df.views      # virtual column, no copy
print(df.mean(df.ratio), df.count())

explainer.inAi: Handy for quick statistics and filtering over huge tabular datasets before sampling a training set.
explainer.jsNote: Vaex is a Python library with no official JavaScript or TypeScript package; call it from a Python service if your app is written in JavaScript.
